"A credible scaling path would combine deeper ultimate-customer relationships, additional trained delivery teams and automation that reduces cost without giving all savings away. The proposed software budget is ₹4.43 crore and planned IT equipment about ₹3.92 crore. By June 2026, monitoring showed ₹1.63 crore software utilization and ₹3.92 crore equipment utilization, with ₹2.80 crore of software funds still unused. A minimum ₹2.00 crore software spend had been planned by March 2026; the monitoring agency identified delay but not an object deviation because the prospectus permits later deployment. Spending is not commissioning, and commissioning is not a proven return. [S01, S18]

The runway cannot be equated with a large global outsourcing market. Prodocs' accessible demand is limited by customer relationships, delivery quality, concentration, data security and sales capacity. Service scale can be less physically constrained than a factory, yet receivables and payroll still absorb funding. Receivables rose to ₹29.1716 crore and closing receivable days reached about 193, even though revenue is only ₹55.2317 crore. Loans of ₹10.7928 crore, security deposits, software, goodwill and office commitments make this less cash-light than the label IT services suggests. [S02]

The operating model therefore includes incremental receivables, other operating working capital, ordinary capex and completion of software spending. It does not assume that depreciation equals maintenance capex, that all new investment earns the historic margin, or that credit is available just because a bank balance or borrowing existed. The proposed remaining eData acquisition, separate subsidiary assistance and Gemini support compete for capital rather than automatically extend an organic runway. GQS is NS because four of its five factors cannot be scored reliably; its missing-weight range does not imply supported growth quality."

"All amounts in the historical table are ₹ crore, and each row retains its accounting vintage. The FY23 original uses thousands despite some inconsistent captions. Standalone, IPO-restated and FY26 consolidated comparatives are not silently spliced into one supposedly homogeneous earnings or cash series. FY26 reported owner PAT is ₹9.4572 crore after ₹0.9570 crore non-controlling interests; consolidated PAT before NCI is ₹10.4142 crore. Operating EBIT excluding other income is ₹13.6823 crore and EBITDA ₹15.2634 crore, or 27.64% of revenue. Other income of ₹1.6730 crore includes ₹1.2125 crore loan interest and ₹0.4032 crore exchange gain. Neither is recurring operating customer revenue. [S02]

Reported profit improvement is not entirely operating scale. Training expense fell from ₹8.8841 crore to ₹5.9049 crore and software expense from ₹1.0216 crore to ₹0.1333 crore, while consolidated employees and the acquisition changed scope. The acquired calendar-year eData accounts show USD5.0989 million revenue but only USD18,965 operating income; reported net income of USD107,622 includes an USD88,655 balance writeback. Those calendar-year management accounts are not a like-for-like April–March audited consolidation bridge and are not mechanically translated into FY26 normalized profit. [S10, S11, S02]

The FY26 cash-flow statement adds minority interest, translation reserve and issue expenses to operating profit. Its numerical total reconciles to the reported closing cash, but the economic classification does not. A matching total is not proof that operating cash has been correctly measured. The table below preserves every disclosed adjustment. Reported CFO is -₹11.2123 crore, reported CFO/PAT before NCI is -1.08×, and CFO less all cash fixed/intangible purchases is -₹23.8317 crore. These are source-defined diagnostics, not normalized owner FCF. Cash purchases of ₹12.6194 crore include ₹3.5603 crore goodwill; excluding goodwill leaves ₹9.0591 crore, still not a clean organic/maintenance split. No invented corrected CFO is substituted. [S02]

The IPO-restated FY23–FY25 CFO totals ₹8.8170 crore against PAT ₹9.8123 crore, or 89.86%. But the restatement separately classified large loans given in investing cash flow, including ₹13.1338 crore in FY25. Original FY25 CFO was -₹9.4024 crore and the subsequent comparative -₹9.4057 crore. One cannot select positive restated CFO while ignoring the financing of non-operating advances, or treat all differences as operating deterioration. The conflict ledger records unresolved residuals after identifying classification changes. [S01, S03, S02]

Receivables include ₹2.4660 crore unbilled revenue. Adding that again would overstate working capital. For the model, opening operating NWC is ₹31.1803 crore: receivables ₹29.1716 plus ₹2.0087 crore of specified vendor/employee/prepaid/other operating advances net of trade payables and employee liabilities. Tax/government balances, loan receivables, accrued loan interest, cash and security deposits are excluded from this narrow operating measure. It is an analytical classification, not the company's own audited NWC subtotal. Ultimate-customer ageing and post-year-end realization must still be supplied. [S02]

Reported cash and bank balances were ₹10.0869 crore, of which cash equivalents were ₹5.2725 crore and other bank balances ₹4.8144 crore. IPO-unspent funds of ₹7.9068 crore and ₹0.0026 crore unclaimed dividends leave at most ₹2.1775 crore unearmarked at March. Some deposits secure borrowing, so this is an upper bound, not unrestricted cash. Non-current deposits of ₹0.5023 crore are not added. June proceeds monitoring shows ₹2.83 crore still earmarked, held in bank/FD instruments, but does not disclose total current free cash. The pre-entry bridge treats every unknown April–October net cash movement as an assumption and exposes ₹0/₹1.72675/₹5/₹10 crore leakage sensitivities. It never presents the March upper bound as observed October cash. [S02, S18]

Gross debt of ₹14.4014 crore is about 0.94× reported operating EBITDA, and EBIT/finance cost about 6.80×. These favorable-looking ratios do not settle liquidity. Disclosed unsecured bank/NBFC rates include 15–18.5%, a ₹0.4514 crore NBFC borrowing is described as 23% and repayable on demand, overdraft terms are around repo plus 3.75%, and director funding is ₹4.2594 crore. The model's 14% blended interest assumption is not a committed refinancing quote. Existing maturity schedules are dated March and do not establish October balances. No undrawn facility is assumed. [S02]

A financing-side invested-capital proxy is owners' equity plus NCI plus debt less all reported cash, identified loans and non-current FD. It rises from ₹10.8901 crore to ₹48.3273 crore. At an analytical 25% tax rate, operating NOPAT rises from ₹4.9058 crore to ₹10.2617 crore. The resulting average-capital ROIC proxy is 34.66%, but one-year incremental return is only 14.31%. Neither is a reliable organic return: acquisition timing, goodwill, translation, capitalized software, current-tax classification and reclassified cash are unresolved. Compared with an illustrative 14–18% nominal operating capital-cost sensitivity, the incremental proxy is not unequivocally value creating. Three- and five-year comparable incremental operating ROIC remain NS because the opening operating-capital bridge is not established; the revenue history alone cannot fill that gap. CAP remains NS. [S01, S02]

Audit coverage below includes full opinions and available annexures, not merely a clean-opinion label. FY20–FY22 originals and IFC reports were reviewed; FY23–FY25 originals, CARO where provided and IFC were reviewed; FY26 standalone and consolidated opinions, CARO, IFC and the secretarial audit with limitation letter were reviewed. Delayed statutory payments, scope wording and restatements remain visible. An unmodified opinion does not resolve these analyst reconciliation questions.

The average-opening/closing receivable-days calculation is also retained, using total revenue as a proxy because credit sales are not separately disclosed. Acquisition timing distorts that average; the closing balance is therefore additionally used for the explicit collection scenarios. Payable days and the cash conversion cycle are ND because compatible credit-purchase denominators are not established; payroll is not treated as inventory purchases. The extended historical dataset retains EBITDA/EBIT proxies, gross-profit and normalized-PAT gaps, FCF purchase definitions, lease/cash limitations and every available EPS/share-count vintage. Original FY24/FY25 basic and diluted EPS use visibly different denominator presentations, so no spurious bonus-adjusted EPS CAGR is calculated."

"At indicative ₹153 and 7,050,000 issued shares, equity capitalization is ₹107.865 crore. Using owner PAT and current shares gives FY26 EPS ₹13.4145 and P/E about 11.41×; dividing by the reported weighted-average EPS ₹15.99 would understate the comparable post-issue P/E. The owner-equity P/B is about 2.16×. A reported-balance EV bridge adds debt and NCI book equity and subtracts all reported cash, producing about ₹117.61 crore and EV/operating EBITDA 7.71×. This is only a cross-check: NCI book value is not market value, restricted cash cannot fund distributions, and stale balance-sheet figures do not establish October EV. [S02, M02]

The explicit valuation uses five annual periods with monthly linked cash checks and an owner-earnings terminal P/E, excludes unverified surplus-cash ownership from its main value, then discounts terminal per-share proceeds to the 15% equity hurdle. It is an equity method: interest and debt repayment are already reflected in earnings and cash, so debt is not subtracted again from terminal P/E value. Rent remains an operating expense; no Ind AS lease debt is fabricated and future rent is not deducted twice. Dividends are zero, so retained cash is not counted both as a distribution and terminal cash. Loans and collateral property are not added as recoverable surplus assets.

All three operating scenarios are illustrative, not supported forecasts. The bear uses -15% first-year revenue then 0%, 3%, 3%, 3%, a 12% EBITDA margin and 8× terminal P/E. The base uses 10% growth, 24% margin and 12× P/E. The bull uses 18% growth, 27% margin and 15× P/E. Tax is 25%, D&A 2.5% of revenue, ordinary capex 4% plus ₹2.80 crore software completion, and the software draw is matched only to earmarked funds. Closing receivable days improve to 190/145/125 in the bear/base/bull by year five, respectively; other NWC scales with revenue. These collection assumptions are economically important, not invisible balancing plugs.

Opening October cash is unknown. For illustration the March unearmarked upper bound is carried forward with zero unknown net change, while the June earmarked balance is carried forward separately. Full pool exercise adds ₹0.35 crore and 350,000 shares at entry. The model then checks a ₹1 crore cash floor and a front-loaded payment stress: half the monthly payments occur before that month's customer receipts. This timing assumption can cause a breach even if month-end cash remains positive. It is intentionally disclosed, not an observed payroll schedule. Unfunded paths stop at their first breach and have no ordinary terminal return.

A separate rescue version, capped at ₹10 crore gross cumulative issuance, issues enough whole shares at a hypothetical ₹91.80 per share, 40% below ₹153, with a 3% fee to preserve the floor at each stressed trough. No lender or investor has committed this funding. A cap failure stops the path with no terminal return. Separately labeled unlimited mathematical counterfactuals illustrate dilution under an extreme guarantee call, not funding availability. Terminal shares, cash, earnings and per-share values are recalculated after every issue. The proposed buyout case pays ₹15 crore, removes the NCI profit proxy after payment, spends a separate ₹15 crore externally at the subsidiary, and advances only incremental Gemini ₹3.27325 crore. The corresponding no-rescue path remains stopped at its earlier cash breach. The guarantee stress is separate from the routine case because the proposal is not already outstanding debt.

NCI attribution is a material model limitation. The current 40% target minority accounts for 9.19% of FY26 group profit. Until subsidiary-level cash and earnings forecasts are available, that group-profit fraction is an explicit proxy for minority participation in normalized PAT and surplus cash. It is not a legal dividend waterfall. The buyout case sets that proxy to zero after payment. Surplus-cash allocation and financing-before-issuance FCFE calculations are retained only as unscoreable diagnostics, not an additional assured owner value or per-legacy-share target. Their ownership and financing claims cannot yet be reconciled. Reported multiples provide the separate valuation cross-check.

Two-way sensitivities vary growth versus terminal P/E and margin versus receivable days. Reverse expectations solve the growth required at ₹153 for 12%, 15% and 18% returns, rerunning working capital and dilution at each trial. Entry-price outputs are therefore conditional model diagnostics, not a recommended buy range. Executability and input confidence prevent assigning R, D or P. Transaction-cost sensitivities of 1%, 3% and 5% are shown separately; actual spreads and market impact are ND."

"Classification: Hold — unresolved / insufficient evidence. Research priority: reconcile accounts, funding and tradability; not eligible for investment consideration or a numerical SME ranking yet. It does not meet the compounder criteria: BQS/GQS are NS, several required factors are below 7 and critical gates remain unresolved. The matrix is not forced onto incomplete aggregates.

This conclusion is not simply expensive or cheap. A price decline may improve hypothetical returns but does not repair cash-flow classification, verify unrestricted cash, approve a transaction or create executable liquidity. Favorable consideration would require a coherent audited cash and acquisition bridge, credible independently supported returns on deployed capital, proof of funded obligations without assumed rescue and reliable BSE trading evidence. Existing holders would additionally need their position size, liquidity constraints, taxes and portfolio context assessed; none is supplied, so no personalized exit count or allocation is invented.

Update rule: rerun the same exact framework and source-vintage bridge when these documents arrive. Keep the prior version and explain any score movement. No trade is executed by this research package."

"Managing director Nidhi Parth Sheth has been associated with the company since incorporation; Abhay Prakash Kapashi is the non-executive chairman. The FY26 report names a five-member board and documents an independent-director resignation on 24 March 2026 and replacement from 31 March, subsequently regularized through the July postal ballot. No adverse reason is inferred merely from a resignation. The annual report shows a 13:1 managing-director pay-to-median-employee ratio and no increase in that director's FY26 remuneration; CFO and company-secretary increases were 26.08% and 9.16%. This does not offset connected capital-allocation risk. [S02, S25]

At 31 March 2026, six promoter/promoter-group holders owned 3,665,000 shares, or 51.9858%; public holders owned 3,385,000 shares. The filing says no promoter pledges, non-disposal undertaking or other encumbrance at that reporting date. Public ownership is not identical to genuinely executable free float, and this is not an October pledge certificate. The source's March statement of no outstanding ESOP predates the later scheme. [S31]

The May/June proposal permits 350,000 options, with committee-determined exercise prices no lower than face value and bounded by the stated market-price formula. No vesting or exercise was reported in the initial announcement. The pool equals 4.96% of issued shares, or 4.73% of the resulting fully diluted shares. The model explicitly assumes full exercise at ₹10 and ₹0.35 crore proceeds; this is a stress convention, not a verified grant or commitment. Historical weighted-average diluted shares are not used as today's share count. [S23, S20]

The 9 October proposals are consequential. Buying the remaining 40% of eData from promoter Manan Kothari for up to USD1.5 million is separate from lending or providing assistance up to another USD1.5 million. The filing's INR approximations differ between an approximately ₹15 crore cover limit and a ₹14.47 crore annexure equivalent; the model uses ₹15 crore each as a stated conservative envelope, not a fixed exchange rate or executed price. Shareholder approval and completion remain conditions. At consolidated level, a loan to a subsidiary is eliminated until the subsidiary spends outside the group; the model recognizes only an explicit external-deployment stress, not both the intercompany loan and the same external spend. [S14]

Gemini Innovations is a related entity through promoter/director relationships. The proposed guarantee is capped at ₹32 crore, with management describing an approximately ₹60 crore building as security. That building is not Prodocs' cash or an independently valued recovery asset, and the guarantee agreement was not entered into at the filing date. A separate loan cap is ₹5 crore, of which ₹1.72675 crore was already advanced. Only the remaining ₹3.27325 crore is a new modeled deployment; whether the outstanding loan overlaps March receivables is unresolved. Calling all ₹5 crore a new future outflow would double count. [S14]

The short-lived 19% Sevasarthi investment was approved in June in a newly incorporated company with no reported turnover. An August sale proposal did not complete with the first buyer; September approval changed the buyer and expected completion within a month. Completion is not assumed by cutoff. This is a small financial item but a useful execution check. Arms-length language in a filing is management's assertion, not independent price validation. [S21, S17, S15]

The FY26 secretarial audit dated 28 August is unmodified, with its accompanying limitation letter expressly excluding verification of financial-record correctness and future viability. Audits and committees are necessary controls, not a substitute for resolving the specific cash and minority-benefit questions. [S02]

The prospectus reports no outstanding company criminal proceedings, material civil litigation or regulatory actions at its own date. It separately discloses civil property disputes involving directors, including proceedings involving Paresh Bhatelia and Hasmukh Mehta, both against and by directors. These are allegations or pending disputes, not adjudicated wrongdoing, and no current-resolution conclusion is inferred. The distinction between company exposure and directors’ other activities is retained; a cutoff-date litigation update is still needed. [S01, printed pp.260–263]

Separately, the prospectus lists eight income-tax cases/demands involving director Hasmukh Gulabchand Mehta totaling ₹172.05 lakh, alongside smaller promoter-entity and senior-management tax demands. These are prospectus-date personal/entity exposures, not established liabilities of Prodocs, and the filing states nil company income-tax, TDS and GST proceedings at that date. No subsequent resolution or adjudicated misconduct is inferred. [S01, printed pp.262–263]"

"Prodocs Solutions is a small, US-facing document-processing and non-voice business-process-outsourcing company, not a pharmaceutical-equipment manufacturer. Its practical strength is an established India delivery operation and domain-specific workflows. The investment case would be a small-service-business expansion or special situation, not an evidence-backed compounder today. The decisive limitation is that acquiring a related-party customer changed the reporting perimeter just as receivables, capital deployment and reported profit expanded. Material cash-flow and accounting disclosures do not reconcile sufficiently for a dependable cash-return score. The 19 October 2026 secondary close of ₹153 is an indicative analytical reference, not a primary-verified executable price. All four gates are Hold — unresolved; BQS, GQS and IAS are NS. A lower price alone would not clear financial reliability, funding or tradability. Written reconciliations, dated unrestricted cash and committed facilities, better organic-growth evidence, and verified BSE trading data would change the research decision. [S01, S02, S14, M02]

This is a research-priority / evidence-repair hold, not an instruction to buy, sell or allocate. No numeric ranking is assigned. Negative modeled cash is not reported as an observed default, and unusual disclosures are not allegations of fraud.

Under the separately hypothetical capped-rescue base case, earnings-only terminal proceeds imply about 5.24% annual return at ₹153, below the 15% hurdle. The no-rescue case stops at its first intraperiod cash-floor breach and has no ordinary return. These are assumption-dependent stress results, not a forecast or evidence of an actual cash default."

"Prodocs earns fees for processing documents and back-office workflows: title-plant indexing, title search/reporting, e-publishing and data conversion, imaging and indexing, finance/accounting support and litigation services. Customers pay for completed activity or work under fixed retainership/service arrangements. Revenue recognition uses completion of service stages or slabs; recorded sales and unbilled balances are not equivalent to collections. India-based staff and apprentices carry out much of the work, while the US presence supplies customer access. Demand depends on customers' transaction volumes and willingness to outsource, not on a disclosed binding order book. [S01, S02]

The company established the wholly owned Prodocs Solutions Inc in January 2025 and acquired 60% of eData Solutions Inc on 30 April 2025. eData was already a major related-party customer; consolidating it removes intragroup sales while bringing in external revenue, assets and 40% non-controlling interests. This is economically different from winning an unrelated customer. eData Services Inc remains a related counterparty, and the prospectus says there was no formal agreement with that entity. Treating all subsequent reported consolidated growth as organic would be wrong. [S01, S02]

The prospectus describes approximately 10 million documents processed annually and 98% accuracy. These are management claims, not independently tested unit-economics evidence. It reported 1,011 employees and apprentices at 31 October 2025, including 581 regular employees and 430 apprentices, with 902 in operations; FY26 annual-report remuneration disclosures count 597 permanent employees at March 2026. Different dates and populations prevent calling the change a 41% headcount reduction. Mumbai is the main delivery base, with Bengaluru backup capacity and a US customer-facing presence. Utilization, billable-hour realization, retention cohorts, unit pricing and contribution per document are ND. The company itself describes conventional manufacturing capacity as inapplicable; this does not remove the need to measure service throughput and productivity. [S01, S02]"

"The cutoff is 20 October 2026 in Asia/Kolkata; the prior trading reference is 19 October 2026. Documents retrieved on 23 October are used only where their dated information predates the cutoff. No later share price or subsequently published financial period enters the thesis. Financial history covers the first March 2019–March 2020 period through FY26. FY26 is the latest annual audited period located; no H1 FY27 result was located by the cutoff. Interim FY26 figures are not treated as a new TTM year.

The issuer is Prodocs Solutions Limited, BSE SME code 544643, symbol PRODOCS, ISIN INE10XK01019. It was incorporated on 12 March 2019, converted to a public company on 13 November 2024 and listed on 15 December 2025. Indian GAAP / Accounting Standards is the policy basis stated in Note 2.01; the inconsistent audit-opinion references to Ind AS require clarification. The five-year analytical horizon runs from 20 October 2026 to 20 October 2031. The nominal INR equity hurdle is 15%, with 12% and 18% sensitivities. These are analyst conventions, not the company's cost of funds. The ₹5 lakh liquidity reference is illustrative, not a suitable position recommendation. [S01, S02]

Confidence is High for identity and the existence of the disclosed transactions, Medium for the reported historical revenue and governance chronology, Low for comparable organic growth, cash quality, incremental returns, actual entry-date funding and executable valuation. Overall investment confidence is Low, determined by these material gaps rather than an average of stronger areas. The dated March shareholding disclosure is not current assurance. No current credit-rating opinion or committed undrawn financing was verified; an Infomerics proceeds-monitoring report is not a credit rating.

Sector/archetype: a profitable IT-enabled service business with concentrated customer access, acquired scope and substantial receivable funding. The framework weights are unchanged. Service throughput, retention, price realization, security and software productivity substitute for factory utilization; absent metrics remain ND."
"The indicative price is not an obviously extreme reported multiple; that alone cannot establish conservative normalized expectations."

"The long pre-listing history is retained rather than discarded. Parent revenue increased from ₹2.7810 crore in FY21 to ₹45.1290 crore in FY26, a 74.60% five-year CAGR. That rate describes the rapid build-out from a small operation; it is not automatically penalized merely for size. The trajectory matters: FY23 added ₹26.6936 crore, FY24 added ₹8.8157 crore, FY25 lost ₹3.6385 crore and FY26 added ₹3.3376 crore. Parent FY23–FY26 CAGR is 7.22%; FY24–FY26 is approximately -0.33%. These alternate windows diagnose deceleration; they do not replace the preferred five-year window opportunistically. [S03–S08, S02]

FY26 consolidated revenue of ₹55.2317 crore exceeds the FY25 comparative by 32.16%, while parent revenue grew only 7.99%. The ₹10.1027 crore gap between FY26 consolidated and parent revenue is a net consolidation difference, not the acquired company's gross sales or an organic-growth estimate. External target revenue, intercompany elimination, acquisition-date scope and currency effects need a single reconciliation. Price, volume and mix are not separately disclosed. Comparable current-perimeter organic five-year or three-year growth is therefore ND and REV remains NS. A mechanical 9 from the parent five-year rate would imply knowledge the source does not provide.

FY26 consolidated first-half revenue of ₹24.4255 crore plus second-half ₹30.8062 crore reconciles to the annual ₹55.2317 crore. Parent halves of ₹20.5371 crore and ₹24.5919 crore reconcile to ₹45.1290 crore. The second-half parent grew about 12.58% against ₹21.8443 crore a year earlier. This is a useful improvement, but one half cannot establish a new multiyear trend. FY20 covers more than a conventional twelve-month period and is excluded from the five-year CAGR endpoint. [S19, S01, S02]"

"The monitoring register sets measurable baselines and evidence requirements rather than generic advice to watch results. Priority goes to financial reconciliation and cash before price targets. A material written reconciliation could reopen CAP/CASH/EARN; a better share price cannot do so by itself. Current BSE tape, lot/restriction data and actual intended position are necessary before any implementation conclusion.\n\nThe next results should distinguish parent organic revenue, acquired external revenue, eliminations, currency and ultimate-customer concentration. They should separately disclose cash available to ordinary operations, pledged balances, proceeds earmarks, debt maturities and committed undrawn headroom. Proposed October transactions need approval, final pricing, cash payment and a minority-benefit rationale, not just another board announcement. Collection delays beyond the modeled 220-day stress or a connected cash call without verified headroom would justify an urgent funding review, not an automatic assertion of default."

"The plausible moat mechanism is embedded workflow knowledge, a trained delivery workforce, information-security processes and the disruption cost of moving a document operation. India delivery costs can help win work, but a low-cost labor model is reproducible. ISO 9001/27001 credentials are entry qualifications rather than proof of pricing power. The prospectus did not establish registered proprietary IP protection for the operating model; trademark applications are not software patents or unique process ownership. No independent market-share study, persistent pricing uplift or cohort-retention evidence was located. [S01]

Customer concentration overwhelms the comfort of a long relationship. Related parties represented 99.46% of FY25 revenue and 98.78% in the prospectus H1 FY26 period. Standalone top-one/top-three FY25 concentration was 83.59%/99.47%; H1 FY26 remained 83.09%/99.27%. Consolidated H1 FY26 top-one, top-three and top-ten exposure was 20.48%, 37.14% and 69.71%, respectively. Consolidation reduced the named related-party share of consolidated sales, but did not prove independent ultimate-client diversification. The lack of a formal eData Services agreement weakens contractual visibility. [S01]

Three relevant benchmarks illustrate what stronger evidence would look like, not a comparable P/E target. eClerx provides analytics, financial operations, digital content and named proprietary workflow products across several industries; Firstsource's FY26 report describes a much larger diversified delivery platform and a long customer partnership; Datamatics reports ₹1,987 crore FY26 revenue, over 300 significant customers and finance/content automation platforms. Their scope, maturity, ownership and service mix differ sharply from Prodocs. We do not transfer their margins, multiples, market shares or retention to this issuer. Official peer sources are used for business-model comparison only. [P01, P02, P03]

AI is two-sided. Automation could improve accuracy and labor productivity, but customers can demand lower prices or move processing in-house, and scaled competitors can invest more. The planned software spend has not yet established monetizable IP or improved cash conversion. A moat upgrade requires independent retention and price evidence, ultimate-customer diversification, demonstrable productivity retained as owner profit, and timely collections."

"The source register links every primary record used, retains retrieval dates and PDF content hashes, and specifies physical page locators where useful. The full originals and temporary text extraction are not redistributed in these source-safe research archives. Authored fact extracts and citations are sufficient for an offline numerical rebuild; readers should revisit linked originals for the complete external documents. A rebuild verifies internal consistency, not the truth of a source.

ND means not disclosed or not located; NM means not economically meaningful; NA means genuinely not applicable; NS means not scoreable. Missing market sessions are ND, never zero. An unavailable BSE response is a retrieval limitation, not evidence that no trade occurred. The interop master corroborates identity and lot size but does not certify BSE surveillance restrictions. Source-safe market rows retain all 60 requested reference dates with missing fields and an explicit calendar limitation.

Open questions: Which accounting framework legally governs FY26 and why does the opinion use another vocabulary? How do the cash-flow NCI, translation reserve and issue-cost lines reconcile to acquisitions, equity and actual bank movements? Why do original, restated and comparative CFO series differ after loan classifications? What explains foreign-currency receivables exceeding total receivables and the rent-note mismatch? What were actual unrestricted cash, pledged deposits, overdue receivables, loan recoverability and undrawn committed facilities on 20 October? What ultimate customers, pricing and collections support organic growth? What independent valuation and benefits support the related-party buyout, assistance and guarantee? What is the final option grant/exercise schedule? What is the current BSE lot, trade-to-trade/surveillance/circuit status and actual 60-session execution capacity?

Material assumptions are published in the model: nominal INR, 15% hurdle, 25% tax, stated collection paths, ordinary and software capex, 14% debt interest, disclosed March maturities rolled forward as an illustration, ₹1 crore cash floor, front-loaded payment stress, zero unknown pre-entry net cash change, full option exercise at ₹10 and hypothetical rescue at ₹91.80 with 3% costs. None is a funding commitment. No scenario probability is assigned, no average of scenario IRRs is labeled a portfolio return, and no post-cutoff price is used."

"The strongest counterargument to the bullish story is that reported growth increasingly reflects bringing a connected customer inside the group and deploying capital beyond ordinary service delivery, while cash realization and minority economics remain difficult to verify. If the acquisition genuinely strengthens ultimate-customer access and collections normalize, this concern could be disproved. At present, neither a clean audit opinion nor a low headline P/E supplies that evidence.

A correlated failure can combine slower collections, AI-driven price pressure, software overspend, an inability to renew expensive debt, cash transfers to connected entities and a guarantee claim. The guarantee is modeled at ₹0, ₹8 and ₹32 crore, with separate delayed collateral recoveries of ₹0, ₹16 and ₹32 crore. Even full eventual recovery does not fund the earlier call. The model never nets a management-valued ₹60 crore building against today's debt or asserts that the issuer owns it. Equity rescue occurs before the modeled shortage and permanently expands the share base; absent rescue, ordinary returns cease at the first breach.

Impairment risk is High on available evidence, but actual insolvency is not established. Shareholders can lose through adverse dilution or impaired earning power even if a company remains legally solvent and the quoted price later rebounds. A liquidating broker quote is not recovery value. The key thesis-break variable is dated unrestricted cash plus verifiable collections relative to unavoidable obligations and connected cash commitments. New borrowing can bridge timing only if committed and affordable; it cannot fix uneconomic capital allocation. [S02, S14, S18]"

"There are exactly 13 canonical factors: GOV, MOAT, REV, DUR, CAP, CASH, BAL, EXEC, EARN and IAS factors R, D, P, L. Integer judgments apply only where material evidence supports them. Missing factors are NS, not zero, five or peer averages. BQS and GQS retain their original weights without renormalization. IAS reuses final BQS at exactly 25%; it does not add cash quality or growth again. Bounds below are mathematical missing-factor bounds, not investable estimates, confidence intervals or substitutes for a score.

GOV, MOAT, DUR, BAL and EXEC are each 4/10, with Medium confidence. Historical high-score rules would cap Medium-confidence factors at 8, but that cap is not binding here. REV is NS because current consolidated organic growth cannot be isolated, not because this is a recent IPO or a small base. CAP, CASH and EARN are NS because the necessary capital/cash/earnings series are materially unreconciled. R, D and P are NS because a hypothetical rescued valuation is not a supported investment model; L is NS because market observations are missing. No misconduct or insolvency override is asserted. G1 and G3 Holds do not become evidenced Fails. The persistent CASH/CAP ≤3 cap is not triggered by NS.

A one-point change in GOV or MOAT moves a completed BQS by 0.20; DUR by 0.10; BAL or EXEC by 0.08. These judgment sensitivities are subordinate to the missing-factor ranges. The raw score, missing weight, weighted contribution and cap tests are retained in the canonical data. Decimal arithmetic and half-up display rounding are used; classification would use unrounded final values.

The local ±1-point sensitivity is not always linear after overrides: reducing GOV from4 to3 would activate the governance ceiling of3 for BQS/IAS, while the currently assigned4 does not. This is a separate judgment-risk scenario, not an applied cap."

"These are feasibility calculations, not price targets. Five times in five years requires 37.97% annual price growth; ten times in five years requires 58.49%, over seven years 38.95%, and over ten years 25.89%. The tables solve the required revenue growth under 24% EBITDA margin, 145 receivable days, ordinary capex, tax, debt service, full option exercise, rescue dilution subject to a ₹10 crore gross cap where needed and terminal P/E of 8× or 12×. Lower terminal multiples are deliberately included. A target without a feasible sign-changing bracket returns NS, never the numerical search ceiling; funding can make value non-monotonic in growth.\n\nPer-share growth is not identical to business growth: revenue, owner margin, share count and valuation all matter. The starting issued-share EPS is used consistently, and share issuance reduces the legacy holder's claim. Prodocs has a fast early history but almost flat FY24–FY26 parent revenue, unproven software productivity and no validated accessible-market-share denominator. Required market share is ND rather than invented from a broad outsourcing TAM. Without evidence that the needed revenue, collections and reinvestment returns are achievable, both 5× and 10× outcomes are Speculative / unsupported. A mathematically solvable rescue case is not commercially funded or operationally demonstrated."
